description:
LEFT UNFINISHED 2026-08-11 by the op-fm5 O(1) recurrence work. Everything else in op-fm5 verified; this one gate did not finish.

WHAT WAS VERIFIED:
  cargo check --workspace --lib --tests            -> exit 0, no errors
  cargo test --release -p chem-eng...              -> 21 passed, 0 failed
  cargo test --release -p teh-o-prke --lib --tests -> 28 passed, 0 failed
WHAT WAS NOT:
  cargo test --release -p tuas_boussinesq_solver --lib --tests
  Started, ran ~70 minutes wall clock (2.5+ hours CPU, ~920% CPU, actively progressing, NOT hung), then was killed to free the cargo build lock at end of session. NO RESULT WAS OBTAINED -- do not read this as a pass or a fail.

TO RESUME: just run it. Budget well over an hour; consider --no-fail-fast and capturing per-test output rather than piping through tail, so a partial run is still informative.

RISK ASSESSMENT (why this is P2 and not P0): the chem-eng change is a cost change, not a physics change. The summed controller output over six benchmark runs of 40k-80k steps was IDENTICAL before and after to the printed 3 decimal places (e.g. 17175484.304 in both). The only intended numerical difference is that the old code discarded exp(-20) = 2.06e-9 of each step response on retirement and the new code carries it, so any TUAS assertion tighter than about 1e-9 relative on a PID-driven quantity is the only plausible failure mode. TUAS regression tolerances are typically far looser than that. Still needs the actual run.

Blocks closing op-fm5.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
GATE SATISFIED 2026-08-11. The TUAS suite completed on a run that was allowed to finish:

  cargo test --release -p tuas_boussinesq_solver --lib
  test result: ok. 323 passed; 0 failed; 46 ignored; 0 measured; finished in 2959.84s

That is 49 minutes wall-clock, and it ran while a second unrelated TUAS test binary was executing concurrently on the same machine. So the two earlier ~70-minute runs that were killed were not hung — they were simply not given enough time, which is exactly why this bead insisted a killed run is neither a pass nor a fail.

This also confirms the CLAUDE.md guidance added today: these tests must run in parallel and need a generous timeout or a background run. A default 120 s command timeout is off by a factor of twenty-five.

Note the 46 ignored are pre-existing and were not investigated here. Recommend closing this bead once the maintainer has eyeballed the number, and separately checking whether any of those 46 should be running.
